instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: A title-winning centre-forward in his first English season: physically overwhelming and a real creator with his back to goal, but the finishing and decision-making were years from the player of 2009.
Twenty league goals and the Golden Boot; the season the hold-up play and the finishing arrived together.
A knee problem cost him most of the season; a dip in availability rather than in ability.
Twenty-nine goals, a second Golden Boot and the double; world class by any reading.
Malaria in November and eleven league goals after twenty-nine the year before; the physical dominance came and went with his health.
A genuinely good shot-stopper carrying a lower-half side; above the Bryan Gunn anchor, well below the elite keepers of the era.
Six goals in 546 minutes after a January arrival; an Ajax Champions League winner and Olympic gold medallist, rated on that rather than the cameo.
Six starts at 32 for a relegated Portsmouth; a substitute by then and below the standard of the division.
No league goal in seven top-flight seasons; a functional left-back whose value was delivery from wide. Would not be in a modern squad.
Every league minute for a West Ham side that finished seventh.
Two Championship seasons in between; back up with West Ham at 31 and a fringe defender by then.
Joined Blackburn from Coventry in March 1993.
Sixteen goals from wide right in a sixth-placed side and a Scotland regular at the World Cup; his best season.
Thirty-three and twelve starts; the pace that carried his game had gone.
Three years on from the Tottenham rows; thirty-three starts in a cup-final side and the best form of his career.
Eighteen, played out of position at left-back, and still the quickest and most direct player on the pitch at times. Rated on evident top-flight ability, not on output.
Nineteen, and already the most inventive player in the side.
A first full season as an attacking wide man rather than a full-back: five goals and six assists for a side that created almost nothing else.
Arrived from Major League Soccer in January and was immediately Blackburn’s best defender: strong, brave and a genuinely good organiser.
Thirty-seven starts at nineteen; the pace was already top-flight, the rest of the game was not yet.
Clearly the best young player in a relegated Blackburn side; rated as an 18-year-old, well below the England-capped player of 2002.
Three years on from a teenage debut season: by 21 he was the creative centre of the Blackburn side and close to the England team.
Nine starts; the first of the injury-wrecked seasons that defined the rest of his career.
Nine goals in twenty starts, the one late season where the injuries left him alone.
Eleven starts; a knee injury cost him most of the season.
Three starts at Villa; the knee that had been failing him since 2000 finally reduced him to a squad player.
No goals in 18 starts; the physical game was still there and nothing else was.
Four years and three Rangers seasons on from his last rated year; back in England at 31 as a fourteen-start squad forward.
Three injury-wrecked seasons at Tottenham followed. The collapse in starts is fitness, but he did genuinely decline as a defender.
A January loan who was immediately the best passer in a side that finished fourth. Half a season, but the quality was unmistakable.
Nine goals and nine assists from midfield for a sixth-placed Everton; the best season of his career and clearly above the Barry anchor.
Eleven starts on the way back from a cruciate injury; six goals says the delivery survived, the eleven starts say the legs had not yet.
Rated as the same footballer who started the Arsenal season a few weeks later, not lifted for the World Cup medal.
An undemonstrative but excellent screening midfielder and a World Cup winner; a clear starter in an all-time great side.
A stress fracture in the back cost him most of the second half of the season; rated on the player, not the availability.
Displaced by Flamini at thirty; still a first-rate screening midfielder, no longer an automatic starter.
An 18-year-old regular in a relegated side; rated as the prospect, not the long career that followed.
Eight years on from his rated Manchester City season; an established combative Premier League midfielder by this point, hence the step up from 68.
Technically the best player at the club; the output never matched what he could do with a ball.
Twenty-nine starts for a Bradford side relegated with twenty-six points, on famously enormous wages; the touch was still there, the effect was not.
Split between Middlesbrough and Derby; the same player at both.
Split between Middlesbrough and Derby; the same player at both.
Twenty, signed in January, and already an aggressive, front-footed defender who would start in the Premier League for a decade.
A first full season as a starter, and immediately the more reliable half of the partnership.
The centre-half of a side that finished fourth; brave, well organised, and still short of pace against a runner.
PFA Player of the Year; reading and recovery of a genuinely elite defender.
Thirty-six and barely able to train; the reading of the game was intact, the body was not.
Seven starts; injury rather than a fall in level.
Past his peak but still a top-class finisher and the leading scorer.
Three goals in 34 starts at Leeds. Not a barren run for a still-good striker; the finishing itself had gone.
Sixteen starts at Southampton at 29; two years on from his last rated season and no longer a first pick anywhere.
Marginalised under Kenny Dalglish and reduced to 20 starts.
PFA and FWA Player of the Year. Elite one-v-one dribbler and crosser; held short of 90 by how little he offered without the ball.
Thirty-three, fourteen starts and a peripheral figure at Villa; a five-point drop that is age and marginalisation together.
The Real Madrid season that made the role famous; the same footballer Chelsea bought a year later, so the same number.
The best defensive midfielder in the world in these years and the reason the position carries his name; positioning and interception at a level nobody else in the league approached.
The screen in front of a title-winning defence that conceded fifteen league goals; world class, a rung below Lampard (90) only because his contribution is the harder one to see.
Thirty-four and rotated; the reading of the game is intact, the legs are not.
Seven goals in nineteen starts that kept West Ham up almost single-handedly; the ability was already close to elite before the output caught up.
Twenty-three league goals as the whole of a City attack that had not yet been built around anyone else.
Twenty league goals, the captaincy, and the best player in a side that finished third.
A genuine Premier League left-back - fit, sound defensively, limited going forward.
Six goals from midfield in a relegated side; the season that earned the Leeds move.
Thirty-five starts for a relegated City; his last full season before the knee gave way.
A broken ankle in January cost him half the season; before and after it he was already one of the best long passers in the league at 22.
His best Liverpool season and the one Real Madrid bought.
On loan at 19 and clearly the most gifted crosser in a relegated side, without yet the consistency to be more than that.
His peak: thirty-seven starts, an England cap and the delivery that got him the Tottenham move.
Out of the side within eighteen months of the transfer, and the decline is real rather than tactical.
A difficult first English season spent adapting to the physical demands; the technique and movement that made him a 90 were already visible in seven assists.

Footballer of the Year, and the best player in the division until a cruciate rupture in March ended his season; nine goals and fifteen assists from 27 starts. Seven points up on his adaptation season, which is what the year merited.
Fourteen league goals from 21 starts in the season after a cruciate rupture; the pace never fully returned, the finishing and the timing more than covered for it.
World class that season — fourteen goals and eight assists from the left in an unbeaten side.
Thirty-one and a step slower in his last Arsenal season, but still creating at a level almost nobody in the league reached.
Twelve league goals from 859 minutes, mostly from the bench. Rated on finishing ability, not on the limited starting role behind Yorke and Cole.
Seventeen league goals from 23 starts, his best return over a full season; finishing of a genuinely elite standard even while rotated.
Used wide and off the bench before the knee trouble that ended his career took hold; no league goals, but the fall is one of role and fitness rather than ability.
Back from two lost years at thirty-three; the finishing was untouched, the movement around it was not.
